V16-17 keep the KJV's words of Ruth: Whither thou goest, I will go.

verses.text: Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a famine (no food) in the land. And a certain man of Bethlehemjudah went to sojourn (live for a while) in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his 2 sons.

And the name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the name of his 2 sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehemjudah. And they came into the country of Moab, and continued there.
And Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died. And Naomi was left, and her 2 sons.
And they took them wives of the women of Moab. The name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth. And they dwelt (lived) there about 10 years.
And Mahlon and Chilion died also both of them. And the woman was left of her 2 sons and her husband.

Then Naomi arose (got up) with her daughters in law, so that she might return from the country of Moab. For she had heard in the country of Moab how the LORD had visited (cared for) His people in giving them bread.
So Naomi went forth (out) out of the place where she was, and her 2 daughters in law with her. And they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
And Naomi said to her 2 daughters in law: Go, return each to her mother's house. The LORD deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead, and with me.
The LORD grant you that you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband. Then Naomi kissed them. And they lifted up their voice, and wept.
And they said to Naomi: Surely we will return with you to your people.
And Naomi said: Turn again, my daughters. Why will you go with me? Are there yet any more sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?
Turn again, my daughters, go your way. For I am too old to have a husband. If I should say: I have hope, if I should have a husband also to night, and should also bear (give birth to) sons,

Would you tarry (wait) for them till they were grown? Would you stay for them from having husbands? No, my daughters. For it grieves me much for your sakes that the hand of the LORD is gone out against me.
And they lifted up their voice, and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother in law. But Ruth clave (held tight) to her.
And Naomi said: Look, your sister in law is gone back to her people, and to her gods. Return after your sister in law.

And Ruth said: Intreat (beg) me not to leave you, or to return from following after you. For whither (where) you go, I will go. And where you lodge (stay), I will lodge (stay). Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
Where you die, will I die, and there will I be buried. The LORD do so to me, and more also, if anything but death part you and me.
When Naomi saw that Ruth was stedfastly minded (firmly decided) to go with her, then she left speaking to her.
So the 2 of them went until they came to Bethlehem. And it came to pass, when they were come to Bethlehem, that all the city was moved about them, and they said: Is this Naomi?
And Naomi said to them: Call me not Naomi (pleasant). Call me Mara (bitter). For the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
I went out full, and the LORD has brought me home again empty. Why then call me Naomi (pleasant), seeing the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted (hurt) me?
So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter in law, with her, which returned out of the country of Moab. And they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

verses.text: And Naomi had a kinsman (relative) of her husband's, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech. And his name was Boaz.

And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi: Let me now go to the field, and glean (pick up the leftover) ears of corn (grain) after him in whose sight I shall find grace (kindness). And Naomi said to her: Go, my daughter.

And Ruth went, and came, and gleaned (picked up leftover grain) in the field after the reapers (harvest workers). And her hap (chance) was to light on (come to) a part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the kindred (family) of Elimelech.
And look, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said to the reapers (harvest workers): The LORD be with you. And they answered him: The LORD bless you.
Then Boaz said to his servant that was set over the reapers (harvest workers): Whose damsel (young woman) is this?
And the servant that was set over the reapers (harvest workers) answered and said: It is the Moabitish damsel (young woman from Moab) that came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab.

And she said: I pray you (please), let me glean (pick up leftover grain) and gather after the reapers (harvest workers) among the sheaves (bundles). So she came, and has continued even from the morning until now, except that she tarried (rested) a little in the house.
Then Boaz said to Ruth: Hear, my daughter. Do not go to glean (pick up leftover grain) in another field, neither go from here, but abide (stay) here fast (close) by my maidens (young women workers).

Let your eyes be on the field that they reap (harvest), and go after them. Have I not charged (told) the young men that they shall not touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the vessels (jars), and drink of that which the young men have drawn.

Then Ruth fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said to Boaz: Why have I found grace (kindness) in your eyes, that you should take knowledge of (notice) me, seeing I am a stranger (foreigner)?

And Boaz answered and said to her: It has fully been showed me all that you have done to your mother in law since the death of your husband. And how you have left your father and your mother, and the land of your nativity (birth), and are come to a people which you knew not before.
The LORD recompense (reward) your work, and a full reward be given you of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings you are come to trust.

Then Ruth said: Let me find favour in your sight, my lord. For you have comforted me, and for that you have spoken friendly to your handmaid (servant), though I am not like one of your handmaidens (women servants).

And Boaz said to her: At mealtime come here, and eat of the bread, and dip your morsel (piece of bread) in the vinegar (sour wine). And she sat beside the reapers (harvest workers). And Boaz reached her parched corn (roasted grain), and she did eat, and was sufficed (full), and left.

And when Ruth was risen up to glean (pick up leftover grain), Boaz commanded his young men, saying: Let her glean (pick up grain) even among the sheaves (bundles), and reproach her not (do not shame her).
And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, so that she may glean (pick) them, and rebuke her not (do not scold her).
So Ruth gleaned (picked up leftover grain) in the field until evening, and beat out that she had gleaned (picked up). And it was about an ephah (about 5 gallons) of barley.

And Ruth took it up, and went into the city. And her mother in law saw what she had gleaned (picked up). And Ruth brought forth (out), and gave to her that she had reserved (saved) after she was sufficed (full).

And her mother in law said to her: Where have you gleaned (picked up grain) to day (today)? And where did you work? Blessed be he that did take knowledge of (notice) you. And Ruth showed her mother in law with whom she had worked, and said: The man's name with whom I worked to day (today) is Boaz.

And Naomi said to her daughter in law: Blessed be he of the LORD, who has not left off His kindness to the living and to the dead. And Naomi said to her: The man is near of kin (closely related) to us, one of our next kinsmen (closest relatives).
And Ruth the Moabitess said: He said to me also: You shall keep fast (close) by my young men, until they have ended all my harvest.
And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter in law: It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his maidens (young women workers), so that they meet you not in any other field.

So Ruth kept fast (close) by the maidens (young women workers) of Boaz to glean (pick up leftover grain) to the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest. And she dwelt (lived) with her mother in law.

verses.text: Then Naomi her mother in law said to Ruth: My daughter, shall I not seek (look for) rest for you, so that it may be well with you?

And now is not Boaz of our kindred (family), with whose maidens (young women workers) you were? Look, he winnows (separates the grain from the chaff) barley to night in the threshingfloor (place where grain is beaten out).

Wash yourself therefore, and anoint (put perfumed oil on) yourself, and put your raiment (clothing) upon you, and go down to the floor (threshing floor). But do not make yourself known to the man, until he shall have done eating and drinking.
And it shall be, when he lies down, that you shall mark (notice) the place where he shall lie. And you shall go in, and uncover his feet, and lay down. And he will tell you what you shall do.
And Ruth said to her: All that you say to me I will do.
And Ruth went down to the floor (threshing floor), and did according to all that her mother in law bade (told) her.

And when Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry (happy), he went to lie down at the end of the heap of corn (grain). And Ruth came softly (quietly), and uncovered his feet, and laid her down.
And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was afraid, and turned himself. And look, a woman lay at his feet.

And Boaz said: Who are you? And she answered: I am Ruth your handmaid (servant). Spread therefore your skirt (the edge of your cloak) over your handmaid (servant), for you are a near kinsman (close relative).
And Boaz said: Blessed be you of the LORD, my daughter. For you have showed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, because you followed not young men, whether poor or rich.
And now, my daughter, fear not. I will do to you all that you require (ask). For all the city of my people does know that you are a virtuous (good and honorable) woman.
And now it is true that I am your near kinsman (close relative). However, there is a kinsman (relative) nearer than I.

Tarry (stay) this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform to you the part of a kinsman (relative), well, let him do the kinsman's part. But if he will not do the part of a kinsman (relative) to you, then will I do the part of a kinsman (relative) to you, as the LORD lives. Lie down until the morning.
And Ruth lay at his feet until the morning. And she rose up before one could know another. And Boaz said: Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor (threshing floor).
Also Boaz said: Bring the vail (shawl) that you have upon you, and hold it. And when she held it, he measured 6 measures of barley, and laid it on her. And she went into the city.
And when Ruth came to her mother in law, Naomi said: Who are you, my daughter? And Ruth told her all that the man had done to her.
And Ruth said: These 6 measures of barley he gave me. For he said to me: Go not empty to your mother in law.
Then Naomi said: Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter will fall (turn out). For the man will not be in rest, until he have finished the thing this day.

verses.text: Then Boaz went up to the gate, and sat him down there. And look, the kinsman (relative) of whom Boaz spoke came by, to whom he said: Ho, such a one (friend)! Turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.
And Boaz took 10 men of the elders of the city, and said: Sit down here. And they sat down.
And Boaz said to the kinsman (relative): Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, sells a parcel (piece) of land, which was our brother Elimelech's.

And I thought to advertise (tell) you, saying: Buy it before the inhabitants (people living here), and before the elders of my people. If you will redeem (buy back) it, redeem (buy back) it. But if you will not redeem (buy back) it, then tell me, so that I may know. For there is none to redeem (buy back) it beside you, and I am after you. And he said: I will redeem (buy back) it.
Then Boaz said: What day you buy the field of the hand of Naomi, you must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance (property).

And the kinsman (relative) said: I cannot redeem (buy back) it for myself, lest (or else) I mar (ruin) my own inheritance (property). You redeem (buy back) my right to yourself, for I cannot redeem (buy back) it.

Now this was the manner (custom) in former time in Israel concerning redeeming (buying back) and concerning changing, to confirm all things: a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour. And this was a testimony (proof) in Israel.
Therefore the kinsman (relative) said to Boaz: Buy it for yourself. So he drew off his shoe.
And Boaz said to the elders, and to all the people: You are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi.

Moreover (also) Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance (property), so that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren (brothers), and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses this day.

And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said: We are witnesses. The LORD make the woman that is come into your house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel. And do worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Bethlehem.
And let your house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare (gave birth to) to Judah, of the seed (children) which the LORD shall give you of this young woman.
So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife. And when he went in to her, the LORD gave her conception (made her pregnant), and she bare (gave birth to) a son.
And the women said to Naomi: Blessed be the LORD, which has not left you this day without a kinsman (redeemer), so that his name may be famous in Israel.
And he shall be to you a restorer of your life, and a nourisher (one who cares for you) of your old age. For your daughter in law, which loves you, which is better to you than 7 sons, has born him.
And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom (lap), and became nurse (caretaker) to it.
And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying: There is a son born to Naomi. And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
Now these are the generations (family line) of Pharez: Pharez begat (became the father of) Hezron,
And Hezron begat (became the father of) Ram, and Ram begat (became the father of) Amminadab,
And Amminadab begat (became the father of) Nahshon, and Nahshon begat (became the father of) Salmon,
And Salmon begat (became the father of) Boaz, and Boaz begat (became the father of) Obed,
And Obed begat (became the father of) Jesse, and Jesse begat (became the father of) David.
